questions.q: What is the main advantage of pathlib's Path object over the older os.path string functions?
options: Path objects run faster than strings in every case
Path objects let you join paths with / and call readable methods like .exists() and .name
Path objects can only be used on Linux
Path objects automatically delete old files
questions.explain: pathlib represents a path as an object with methods, so joining with / and calling .exists(), .name, or .glob() reads more clearly than the equivalent os.path function calls.

questions.q: Why should you open files using a `with` block instead of calling open() and close() manually?
options: with blocks run faster than open()/close()
with blocks guarantee the file is closed even if an error occurs inside the block
with blocks are required syntax in Python 3
with blocks automatically convert the file to read-only
questions.explain: A with block is a context manager — it closes the file automatically when the block ends, even if an exception happens partway through, preventing leaked file handles.

questions.q: What is the difference between Path.glob('*.log') and Path.rglob('*.log')?
options: glob searches recursively; rglob only searches the top-level directory
glob only matches one file; rglob matches many
glob searches only the given directory; rglob searches that directory and all its subdirectories
There is no difference between them
questions.explain: glob() matches a pattern within a single directory level, while rglob() ("recursive glob") walks every subdirectory as well.

questions.q: Which shutil function would you use to relocate an old log file into an archive directory?
options: shutil.copy
shutil.move
shutil.rmtree
shutil.chmod
questions.explain: shutil.move relocates a file (or directory) to a new location. shutil.copy duplicates it instead of moving it, and shutil.rmtree deletes an entire directory tree.

questions.q: What does os.walk() return for each directory it visits?
options: Just a list of filenames
A tuple of (dirpath, dirnames, filenames)
A single Path object
The total disk usage of that directory
questions.explain: os.walk() yields a (dirpath, dirnames, filenames) tuple for every directory under the starting path, which is why it's typically used with a nested for loop.
